title: Kestrel and the Choir
premise: Odile Almeida maps realms that exist only in memory, bound to a valley where magic cannot cross. When the crown's witch-hunt sweeps the borderlands, Odile and the ragtag found family they've gathered — a disgraced royal archivist, a mute choirgirl whose songs hold spells, and a deserter knight — are dragged into the capital. There Odile discovers the king is not the tyrant he appears to be: he is a prisoner inside his own body, and the thing wearing his crown is a memory-eating entity the crown itself created. To free him, Odile must sacrifice the one thing they cannot replace — their own memories of the valley and the people they love — and in the end, they unbind the king and defeat the entity, waking with a blank map of their own past and a family who chooses to remember for them.
about_author: Freya Delacroix is the pen name of a former archival restorer who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. They write fantasy about the weight of what we choose to keep, and live somewhere deliberately unmapped.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile maps the memory-realm of the Choir from the safety of the magicless valley, sketching a world they've never walked. The crown's heralds arrive announcing a gift-hunt, and their found family must flee that night. Beat: the quiet ache of a life about to be uprooted.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash Roads
chapters.summary: Deserter knight Bram's POV. The family escapes through borderlands where hunted gifted folk burn their own names to hide. Bram teaches Odile that loyalty sometimes means lying to the people you love. Beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Girl Made of Hymns
chapters.summary: Choirgirl Sef's POV. Sef, mute, communicates through spell-song; she reveals she has heard the king's true voice crying out inside the realm Odile maps. The family realizes the tyrant is a prisoner. Beat: wonder and dread entwined.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Confession
chapters.summary: Archivist Maren's POV. Maren admits she helped the crown create the entity decades ago — a memory-harvester meant to erase dissent that outgrew its leash. Her guilt fractures the family's trust. Beat: betrayal, and the question of whether truth or loyalty binds them.

chapters.title: The City of Borrowed Faces
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The family infiltrates the capital, where citizens trade memories for safety and the entity's influence is visible in blank-eyed crowds. Odile maps the palace's memory-architecture from afar. Beat: horror at a city that has forgotten how to want anything.

chapters.title: What the Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Inside the palace, Bram confronts his old commander and learns the hunt is a harvesting operation. Sef is captured singing the king's true name aloud. Beat: the cost of loyalty to a crown that was never worthy of it.

chapters.title: The Choir Beneath the Stone
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Imprisoned in the entity's vault, Sef discovers the harvested memories of thousands still singing, waiting. She begins conducting them toward freedom. Beat: defiant hope in the darkest place.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Odile and Maren's alternating POV. The family breaches the vault as the entity offers Odile a bargain: the king's freedom in exchange for Odile's memories of the valley and everyone in it. Maren offers hers instead; Odile refuses to let her. Beat: love measured against self-erasure.

chapters.title: A Map With No Names
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile gives their memories to the Choir of harvested souls, who turn them into a weapon of remembrance that unmakes the entity. The king wakes, weeping in a body that is finally his own. Odile stands among strangers who call them family. Beat: the climax's terrible, tender cost.

chapters.title: Everything We Kept
chapters.summary: Full ensemble POV. The family returns to the valley with the freed king, who abdicates in favor of a council of the once-harvested. Odile cannot remember them, but they have written it all down — every chapter of Odile's life, kept safe, to be read aloud until memory grows back. Beat: found family as the archive that holds you.
